title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self: Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self

questions.question: In the comparison, how much money did the first servant get?
questions.answer: He got twenty gold pieces.

questions.question: What was the first servant told to do with the money?
questions.answer: He was told to get clothes made from a certain cloth.

questions.question: How much money did the second servant get?
questions.answer: He got one thousand gold pieces.

questions.question: What else was put in the second servant’s pocket?
questions.answer: A paper with instructions.

questions.question: What should the second servant have done before spending the money?
questions.answer: He should have read the paper.

questions.question: Why would a wise person know the larger amount of money was not just for clothes?
questions.answer: Because fine clothes had already been bought with much less money.

questions.question: What mistake did the second servant make when he looked at the first servant?
questions.answer: He copied him and spent everything on clothes.

questions.question: Did the second servant get better clothes than the first servant or worse clothes?
questions.answer: He got worse clothes.

questions.question: How did the employer react to the second servant’s choice?
questions.answer: He scolded him and punished him.

questions.question: What lesson does this comparison teach about a person’s life?
questions.answer: Life should not be used only for body pleasures and this short world.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens if a person uses life like an animal?
questions.answer: He falls very low.

questions.question: Why is falling that low especially sad for a human being?
questions.answer: Because a human has been given much more than animals.

questions.question: What is the big idea of this comparison?
questions.answer: Human abilities were not given just to chase worldly life.

questions.question: Who gave money to the servants?
questions.answer: Their master gave it.

questions.question: What did the first servant buy with his money?
questions.answer: He bought a nice set of clothes.

questions.question: What shows that the second servant had a different job to do?
questions.answer: He was given much more money and a written note.

questions.question: What does the written note tell us?
questions.answer: It shows he had an important task or business to do.

questions.question: What foolish choice did the second servant make?
questions.answer: He ignored the note and spent all the money on clothing.

questions.question: What kind of cloth did he end up getting?
questions.answer: A poor, low-quality cloth.

questions.question: Was the second servant’s suit equal to his friend’s suit?
questions.answer: No, it was much worse.

questions.question: Why was the master right to be upset?
questions.answer: Because the servant wasted what was given and did not do his real job.

questions.question: In the warning at the end, what should a person not waste?
questions.answer: The gifts and abilities of life.

questions.question: What kinds of things are we warned not to live for?
questions.answer: Body desires and short-lived pleasures.

questions.question: Compared with animals, what can happen to a person who lives this wrong way?
questions.answer: He can become lower than even low animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say we should understand from the story?
questions.answer: That our human powers are for more than animal-like living.

questions.question: In the story, why was twenty gold pieces enough for the first servant?
questions.answer: Because it was enough to buy very good clothing.

questions.question: Why does one thousand gold pieces suggest a bigger purpose?
questions.answer: Because it was far more than needed for clothes.

questions.question: What important clue did the second servant ignore?
questions.answer: He ignored the paper in his pocket.

questions.question: Instead of thinking carefully, whom did the second servant copy?
questions.answer: He copied the other servant.

questions.question: What does this tell us about following others without thinking?
questions.answer: It can lead to foolish choices.

questions.question: How was the second servant’s purchase described compared with the first servant’s?
questions.answer: It was far worse.

questions.question: What do the master’s sharp words and punishment show?
questions.answer: They show the servant had done something very wrong.

questions.question: Who is being warned in the passage after the story?
questions.answer: The self and the friend are being warned.

questions.question: What should people not use their life’s gifts for?
questions.answer: They should not use them only for physical enjoyment.

questions.question: What is this world called in the warning?
questions.answer: It is called short and passing.

questions.question: If a human forgets his higher purpose, how can he end up compared with animals?
questions.answer: He can end up much lower than they are.

questions.question: How many servants are in the comparison?
questions.answer: There are two servants.

questions.question: What was special about the cloth for the first servant’s clothes?
questions.answer: It was a certain cloth chosen for him.

questions.question: What two things did the second servant receive from his master?
questions.answer: He received a large amount of money and a written message.

questions.question: What was the second servant sent to do?
questions.answer: He was sent to take care of some business.

questions.question: What would a sensible person understand right away?
questions.answer: That the big amount of money had a greater use than buying clothes.

questions.question: What did the second servant do wrong before going to the shopkeeper?
questions.answer: He failed to read the instructions.

questions.question: What happened when he spent all the money on one suit?
questions.answer: He wasted the money and got poor clothing.

questions.question: Why was his action called very foolish?
questions.answer: Because he used something important in the wrong way.

questions.question: After the story, what are people told to do?
questions.answer: They are told to wake up and think rightly.

questions.question: What kind of life are we told not to live?
questions.answer: A life only for fleshly pleasure and temporary things.

questions.question: What warning is given about humans who live only for such things?
questions.answer: Even though they were given more, they may sink lower than animals.

questions.question: What was the first servant’s job with the money he received?
questions.answer: To have clothing made.

questions.question: Did the first servant succeed in getting good clothes?
questions.answer: Yes, he got fine clothes.

questions.question: Why was the second servant’s money not meant for the same simple use?
questions.answer: Because it was a much larger amount and came with instructions.

questions.question: What should the second servant have paid attention to in his pocket?
questions.answer: The note from his master.

questions.question: What bad choice did he make at the store?
questions.answer: He spent all the money on clothing.

questions.question: What does the poor suit show about his decision?
questions.answer: It shows his decision was careless and foolish.

questions.question: How did his suit compare with the first servant’s suit?
questions.answer: It was much worse.

questions.question: Why would the master punish him?
questions.answer: Because he wasted the trust given to him.

questions.question: What human problem does the story warn against?
questions.answer: Using life only for worldly fun and body wants.

questions.question: What does the passage say about this worldly life?
questions.answer: It does not last long.

questions.question: Are humans said to have less or more capital than animals?
questions.answer: They are said to have more.

questions.question: If humans use their greater gifts in the wrong way, what can happen?
questions.answer: They can fall lower than animals.

questions.question: What are readers asked to do at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: They are asked to think about the meaning of the comparison.

questions.question: According to the comparison, were human abilities given only for worldly living?
questions.answer: No, they were given for more than that.

questions.question: What did the master tell the first servant to do with twenty gold pieces?
questions.answer: To get a suit made.

questions.question: What made the second servant’s job different from the first servant’s job?
questions.answer: He was given much more money and written directions.

questions.question: What simple step could have saved the second servant from his mistake?
questions.answer: Reading the paper first.

questions.question: Why was it wrong for him to copy the first servant?
questions.answer: Because his own task was different.

questions.question: What was the result of his bad choice?
questions.answer: He wasted the money and got bad clothing.

questions.question: What does the master’s anger teach us about responsibility?
questions.answer: We must use what we are given in the right way.

questions.question: In the warning, what should not rule a person’s life?
questions.answer: Desires of the body should not rule it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about living only for temporary pleasure?
questions.answer: It makes a person live in a very low way.

questions.question: Why is the warning stronger for human beings than for animals?
questions.answer: Because humans have been given greater gifts and abilities.

questions.question: What is the final warning of the passage in simple words?
questions.answer: Do not waste your life on short pleasures, or you will fall very low.
